purpose: Twentieth expanded public source layer focused on route-context semantics that cannot be represented by isolated reaction templates: cross-step condition envelopes, reagent role and atom-contribution semantics, visual scheme to reaction-graph alignment, expert-review calibration, negative-control and decoy-route generation, endpoint-goal context, reaction-scope transfer, and route portfolio diversity or redundancy.

promotion_requirements: manual chemist, process, data-curation, model-validation, reviewer-calibration, endpoint-owner, and project-governance review

explicit cross-step condition envelope, reagent-role/atom-contribution evidence, visual-to-graph alignment, reviewer calibration, decoy/negative-control provenance, endpoint definition, substrate-scope transfer evidence, or route-portfolio rationale before proposal promotion
separate condition-envelope, role-semantics, visual-alignment, review-calibration, negative-control, endpoint-context, substrate-scope, and route-diversity policy

route-specific pH/temperature/solvent/carryover compatibility, atom mapping and reaction role assignment, scheme/SMILES/graph reconciliation, rubric and inter-rater agreement, hard-negative construction, endpoint criteria, functional-group tolerance, and shared-bottleneck or backup-route analysis
safety, legal, copyright, source-license, reviewer-consensus, route-objective, assay-context, and benchmark-governance review where relevant
safety_scope: records intentionally avoid operational quantities, executable procedures, hazardous instructions, scale-up instructions, biological protocols, and unpublished proprietary details

v21 records are route-context and source-policy priors only and must not auto-close routes as stock, validated condition envelopes, validated atom maps, validated visual extractions, final review labels, or executable decoy generators

families.name: Cross-step condition envelope, pH/temperature/solvent carryover, aqueous/organic handoff, cofactor, and protecting-group compatibility policy
families.strategic_principle: Separate single-step feasibility from route-level condition compatibility. Multistep and cascade records need pH, temperature, solvent, cofactor, intermediate stability, carryover, and isolation/handoff evidence before the route can be trusted.

families.name: Reactant/reagent/catalyst role assignment, atom contribution, carrier reagent, sacrificial scaffold, and atom-provenance semantics policy
families.strategic_principle: Separate a named precursor from the atoms and role it contributes. Route meaning changes when a large species is a carrier reagent, sacrificial scaffold, catalyst, solvent, or stock-like reactant; atom provenance and role assignment are strategic source fields.

families.name: Rendered route scheme, text/table extraction, reaction graph, SMILES, atom map, and figure-provenance alignment policy
families.strategic_principle: Separate visual evidence from machine-readable route records. A route scheme, table, or figure becomes a usable source only after image segmentation, structure recognition, role assignment, SMILES/graph reconciliation, and source-file provenance are reviewed.

families.name: Expert review rubric, inter-rater agreement, disagreement adjudication, label drift, and calibration-example policy
families.strategic_principle: Separate a review label from evidence that reviewers apply it consistently. Route-quality, failure, and promotion labels need rubrics, calibration examples, inter-rater agreement, adjudication, and drift checks.

families.name: Negative-control, decoy route, corrupted route, self-loop, hard negative, and benchmark-control generation policy
families.strategic_principle: Separate failure examples that improve a verifier from artifacts that bias evaluation. Negative and decoy route records need construction provenance, hardness controls, label-noise checks, leakage guards, and source-backed failure modes.

families.name: Endpoint-definition, target-vs-analogue, API, impurity, reference standard, probe, demonstration, and route-goal context policy
families.strategic_principle: Separate a molecular structure from the purpose of making it. The same compound can require different source criteria as an API, analogue, impurity standard, reference material, probe, prodrug, demonstration route, or process endpoint.

families.name: Reaction-scope transfer, substrate-class boundary, functional-group tolerance, negative-scope, and analogue-cliff policy
families.strategic_principle: Separate a reaction precedent from the substrate class where it remains trustworthy. Scope transfer records need substrate selection logic, functional-group tolerance, negative examples, steric/electronic boundaries, and analogue-cliff evidence.

families.name: Route diversity, portfolio, backup route, shared bottleneck, redundancy, common-intermediate, and multi-objective route policy
families.strategic_principle: Separate the single best-looking route from a strategically useful route portfolio. Multiple chemically diverse routes can hedge shared bottlenecks, supply risk, scale-up uncertainty, IP constraints, and objective changes.

anchors.name: Condition-envelope anchor with reviewed pH, temperature, solvent, cofactor, intermediate stability, carryover, and handoff compatibility
Role/atom-contribution anchor with reviewed reactant, reagent, catalyst, solvent, carrier, sacrificial scaffold, and atom-provenance evidence
Visual-scheme alignment anchor with reviewed source figure, extracted structures, labels, reaction graph, SMILES, atom map, and role assignment
Expert-review calibration anchor with rubric, calibration examples, inter-rater agreement, adjudication trace, and label-drift checks
Negative-control/decoy anchor with reviewed construction rule, failure mode, hardness, label-noise, leakage, and benchmark-control provenance
Endpoint-goal anchor with reviewed target identity, analogue boundary, API/impurity/probe/standard purpose, assay or specification, and acceptance criteria
Scope-transfer anchor with reviewed substrate class, functional-group tolerance, steric/electronic boundary, negative scope, and analogue-cliff evidence
Route-portfolio anchor with reviewed diverse routes, backup value, shared bottlenecks, common intermediates, supply/IP/process risks, and objective tradeoffs

disconnections.name: Multistep route to condition envelope plus pH, temperature, solvent, cofactor, carryover, and handoff boundary

break_bonds: single-step condition to route-level condition envelope boundary
intermediate handoff to carryover compatibility boundary
forward_logic: separate step precedent from route-level condition compatibility
track pH, temperature, solvent, cofactor, intermediate stability, catalyst tolerance, and isolation or buffer-exchange handoff
flag cascades where each individual step is plausible but the combined condition envelope is not
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Reward multistep routes only when cross-step condition compatibility and handoff evidence are explicit.

evidence.citation: Linear biocatalytic cascade review discusses compatibility of individual reaction steps and pH/temperature suitability across enzymes.
Roadmap for biocatalysis discusses pH, temperature, product, substrate, cofactor, and catalyst incompatibilities in one-pot cascades.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit pH, temperature, solvent, cofactor, carryover, and handoff compatibility

disconnections.name: One-pot or sequential cascade to compartmentalization, isolation, buffer exchange, and route-efficiency policy

break_bonds: one-pot claim to compatibility/compartmentalization boundary
sequential route to isolation and buffer-exchange boundary
forward_logic: separate route telescoping from evidence that catalysts and intermediates can share a vessel or require separation
track concurrent vs sequential mode, compartmentalization, flow cartridge separation, buffer exchange, purification loss, and process complexity
avoid rewarding one-pot claims without compatibility evidence or realistic handoff operations
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Use one-pot and sequential cascade records only when compatibility or separation mode is part of the source.

evidence.citation: Chemical Society Reviews article on chemo/photo-enzymatic cascades discusses concurrent, sequential, and compartmentalized cascade modes.
Continuous-flow biocatalysis review discusses pH/temperature/cofactor incompatibility and buffer-change complexity for cascade processes.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit concurrent/sequential mode, compartmentalization, buffer exchange, isolation loss, and process complexity

disconnections.name: Precursor set to reactant/reagent/catalyst role assignment plus product-atom contribution boundary

break_bonds: named input to reaction-role boundary
product structure to atom-contribution boundary
forward_logic: separate a molecule appearing in a reaction from the role it plays in product construction
track limiting reactant, reagent, catalyst, solvent, internal standard, product atom contribution, and atom mapping
avoid treating a reagent or catalyst as a strategic precursor merely because it is large or purchasable
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Reward precursor records only when role assignment and atom contribution are explicit.

evidence.citation: ORD schema documentation records reaction inputs, roles, identifiers, amounts, conditions, outcomes, and provenance.
Reaction role assignment article describes the challenge of assigning reactant, reagent, and product roles in large reaction data sets.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit role assignment, atom map, product contribution, and provenance

disconnections.name: Large input to carrier reagent or sacrificial scaffold plus contributed-fragment and terminal-audit policy

break_bonds: large input to carrier-vs-product-like boundary
terminal molecule to contributed-fragment boundary
forward_logic: separate input size from whether the input is product-like or a carrier of a small fragment
track atom contribution, leaving scaffold, product-inherited atoms, terminal stock status, and route-audit label
neutralize size-based product-like penalties when atom provenance shows a carrier reagent, and penalize product-like stock shortcuts otherwise
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Classify large inputs using atom provenance and carrier context, not heavy-atom count alone.

risks: carrier reagent mistaken as advanced intermediate

evidence.citation: AutoPlanner cascade report records a large Wittig phosphorane carrier reagent that should not be classified as product-like terminal by size alone.
Chemaxon reaction mapping documentation describes atom mapping as identifying atoms across reactant and product sides.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit contributed fragment, leaving scaffold, atom map, and terminal audit label

disconnections.name: Rendered scheme to extracted structures, labels, SMILES, reaction graph, and role-alignment boundary

break_bonds: visual scheme to machine-readable structure boundary
figure layout to reaction graph and role boundary
forward_logic: separate a rendered route figure from a source record usable by the planner
track figure provenance, segmentation, structure recognition, label assignment, arrow topology, reaction graph, SMILES, and manual correction
avoid promoting visual schemes until molecule identity and reaction roles align with the figure
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Use visual route sources only after scheme-to-SMILES and scheme-to-graph alignment are reviewed.

evidence.citation: ReactionDataExtractor 2.0 constructs reaction-scheme graphs from images and integrates OCR/OCSR engines.
DECIMER.ai describes automated extraction and interpretation of chemical structures into machine-readable representations.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit figure provenance, segmentation, OCSR, label/role assignment, graph alignment, and manual correction

disconnections.name: Local PPTX/PDF scheme to source-file, rendered asset, extracted table, route graph, and manual-redraw alignment policy

break_bonds: local visual source to reviewed route graph boundary
embedded scheme to manual-redraw and file-provenance boundary
forward_logic: separate local visual assets from route-card evidence that can be queried
track PPTX/PDF path, slide/asset ID, extracted text/table, rendered scheme, manual redraw, structure assignment, and reviewer signoff
keep local visual schemes advisory until graph alignment and source provenance are complete
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Treat local PPTX schemes as route-card candidates until visual, graph, and structure alignment are signed off.

risks: route graph not aligned with table

evidence.citation: Local statin route extraction records PPTX-derived route context and embedded scheme limitations.
Integration notes require extracting/redrawing chemical schemes and checking structures, atom mapping, stereochemistry, hazards, and process constraints before template promotion.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: low until source path, rendered asset, graph alignment, structures, stereochemistry, and reviewer signoff are explicit

disconnections.name: Route-quality label to reviewer rubric, calibration examples, inter-rater metric, and adjudication boundary

break_bonds: single reviewer label to rubric/calibration boundary
review outcome to inter-rater/adjudication boundary
forward_logic: separate review labels from evidence that the label process is reliable
track rubric version, calibration examples, reviewer IDs or roles, inter-rater metric, disagreement class, adjudication, and final label
avoid training route-value models on uncalibrated or drifted review labels
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Use human review labels as strong source evidence only when rubric and inter-rater calibration are recorded.

evidence.citation: Kappa statistic review explains interrater reliability and agreement metrics for categorical ratings.
Inter-rater reliability tutorial discusses choosing, computing, interpreting, and reporting reliability statistics.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for rubric version, calibration set, inter-rater metric, adjudication trace, and final label provenance

disconnections.name: Review label stream to label-drift, reviewer disagreement, ambiguity class, and recalibration policy

break_bonds: review label stream to drift-monitoring boundary
disagreement to ambiguity/adjudication boundary
forward_logic: separate a growing label set from evidence that reviewer behavior stayed consistent
track review batch, label distribution, disagreement categories, ambiguous examples, rubric changes, recalibration, and model retraining impact
flag labels collected under shifted rubrics or unadjudicated disagreement
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Down-rank review labels when drift, ambiguity, or rubric changes are not tracked.

risks: ambiguous cases forced into hard labels

evidence.citation: Annotation quality management analysis notes that inter-annotator agreement should be paired with validation and adjudication measures.
Clinical annotation study describes annotation guidelines, annotator expertise, and inter-annotator reliability measurement.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit batch version, disagreement class, rubric revision, recalibration, and adjudication evidence

disconnections.name: Verifier training record to decoy route, hard negative, corrupted route, and label-noise guardrail boundary

break_bonds: negative example to decoy-generation boundary
training control to label-noise and leakage boundary
forward_logic: separate a useful hard negative from a biased or mislabeled artifact
track generation rule, source route, corrupted feature, hardness criterion, overlap with positives, label-noise risk, and benchmark split
avoid training verifiers on decoys that leak labels through trivial artifacts or false-negative chemistry
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Use decoy route records only when construction rule, hardness, label-noise, and leakage checks are explicit.

evidence.citation: DUD-E benchmark describes property-matched decoys as negative controls and discusses benchmark design.
DUD-E bias study shows decoy-selection artifacts can mislead model performance evaluation.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit decoy rule, hardness, label-noise, leakage, and source route provenance

disconnections.name: Failed reaction or route artifact to source-backed negative control plus failure-mode and benchmark-use policy

break_bonds: failed experiment to comparable negative-data boundary
route artifact to benchmark-control boundary
forward_logic: separate negative data that teaches route boundaries from incomparable or incomplete failure records
track attempted substrate, condition context, target endpoint, observed failure mode, comparability to positives, and use in training or evaluation
avoid promoting failures without enough context to distinguish chemistry limits from missing metadata
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Use failed-reaction controls when failure context and positive comparability are explicit.

evidence.citation: Negative chemical data paper discusses failed reactions and negative data for improving chemistry machine-learning models.
Reaction-condition prediction review discusses hard negatives and negative transfer in data-driven reaction modeling.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit failure mode, comparable positive context, metadata completeness, and benchmark-use boundary

disconnections.name: Molecular endpoint to target-vs-analogue, route demonstration, API, impurity, probe, or reference-standard goal boundary

break_bonds: molecular identity to route-goal boundary
target/analogue distinction to acceptance-criteria boundary
forward_logic: separate the structure being made from the purpose of making it
track whether the endpoint is API, analogue, impurity, reference standard, probe, route demonstration, or process intermediate
apply route acceptance criteria that match endpoint goal rather than using one generic success metric
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Require endpoint-goal context before deciding whether a route is successful or source-promotable.

risks: demonstration route judged as API route
probe quality confused with drug quality

evidence.citation: ICH Q3A(R2) guideline covers impurity reporting, identification, and qualification in new drug substances.
Chemical probe quality review distinguishes probe fitness criteria such as potency, selectivity, and target engagement from general compound availability.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit endpoint purpose, target/analogue boundary, acceptance criteria, and assay/specification context

disconnections.name: Endpoint source to reference-standard, probe, API, impurity, or assay acceptance criteria policy

break_bonds: endpoint source to purpose-specific acceptance boundary
assay or specification to route-evidence boundary
forward_logic: separate a route endpoint from the evidence needed for its intended use
track purity, identity, stability, analytical method, biological validation, specification, or demonstration-only status
flag endpoint sources that lack the evidence required for their declared purpose
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Use endpoint-specific evidence gates for standards, probes, APIs, and demonstration routes.

evidence.citation: ICH Q6A guidance covers specifications and acceptance criteria for new drug substances and products.
Probe Miner paper discusses quantitative assessment of potential chemical probes and probe-quality fitness factors.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit declared use, purity/identity/stability, method or assay, and endpoint-specific acceptance criteria

disconnections.name: Reaction precedent to substrate-class, functional-group tolerance, steric/electronic boundary, and negative-scope policy

break_bonds: reaction precedent to substrate-class scope boundary
functional group tolerance to transferability boundary
forward_logic: separate a reported reaction from evidence it transfers to the target substrate class
track scope-set selection, functional-group tolerance, steric/electronic descriptors, excluded substrates, and target-substrate similarity
avoid transferring methods from biased scope tables without negative or boundary examples
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Reward reaction precedents only when substrate-scope transfer and functional-group tolerance are explicit.

evidence.citation: Substrate-selection paper discusses biases in reported substrate-scope studies and strategies for unbiased reaction generality evaluation.
Reaction-scope generality review discusses substrate selection, data acquisition, and analysis for generality-oriented reaction optimization.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit substrate class, scope-set selection, functional-group tolerance, negative examples, and target similarity

disconnections.name: Analogue proposal to scope cliff, failed substrate, out-of-domain functional group, and review-worklist policy

break_bonds: analogue route to scope-cliff boundary
failed substrate to review-worklist boundary
forward_logic: separate close analogue similarity from actual transferability of the reaction
track activity or reactivity cliffs, failed substrate records, out-of-domain functional groups, and reviewer resolution
turn uncertain analogue transfers into review worklist items rather than strong proposal sources
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Down-rank analogue transfers when substrate-scope cliffs or failed examples are not resolved.

evidence.citation: Predictive chemistry review discusses reaction development, substrate-scope assessment, and the role of reaction data in deployment.
Functional-group evaluation kit paper notes limitations in reporting functional-group tolerance and negative findings.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: low unless failed substrates, out-of-domain groups, and reviewer resolution are explicit

disconnections.name: Single best route to chemically diverse portfolio plus backup route, shared bottleneck, and objective-tradeoff boundary

break_bonds: top route to route-portfolio boundary
route cost to diversity and shared-bottleneck boundary
forward_logic: separate the lowest-cost route from a route set that hedges strategic risk
track route diversity, shared intermediates, common bottlenecks, supplier/IP/process risks, backup value, and objective-specific tradeoffs
avoid collapsing search to one route when chemically distinct backups reduce risk
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Reward route pools that expose chemically diverse backups and shared-bottleneck risk.

evidence.citation: Chemical Science article discusses selecting cost-effective yet chemically diverse pathways from computer-generated retrosynthetic plans.
CompRet paper states that CASP programs should provide many synthetic routes to consider optimal and alternative routes.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit route diversity, backup value, shared bottlenecks, and objective-specific tradeoffs

disconnections.name: Route set to common intermediate, shared bottleneck, redundancy, and portfolio-risk policy

break_bonds: route set to common-intermediate boundary
shared bottleneck to redundancy-risk boundary
forward_logic: separate useful shared intermediates from fragile shared bottlenecks
track common intermediate scope, route branching, backup source, supplier or process bottleneck, and diversity across objectives
flag portfolios whose routes look diverse downstream but share the same risky upstream constraint
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Use common-intermediate records only when shared-bottleneck and redundancy risks are explicit.

risks: backup route depends on same supplier

evidence.citation: PaRoutes framework discusses route quality and route diversity metrics for retrosynthesis route prediction benchmarks.
Convergent retrosynthesis planning article discusses identifying shared convergent routes across multiple compounds.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit common-intermediate scope, shared-bottleneck risk, backup source, and objective context

source_notes.summary: The v21 expansion promotes backlog families covering cross-step condition compatibility, role and atom-contribution semantics, visual scheme to graph alignment, expert-review calibration, negative-control and decoy-route generation, endpoint context, substrate-scope transfer, and route portfolio diversity.

V21 records are advisory route-context records. Promotion requires explicit evidence and reviewer approval; they must not turn visual schemes, atom-role guesses, review labels, hard negatives, endpoint contexts, scope transfers, or route portfolios into executable procedures or stock closures by default.
